posts.note: Re-run of a satirical fiction piece (Mordor Inc. board meeting). Forward-looking lines ('where the market is going', 'scale to 10,000 humanoid OneRing platform users in Q1', 'performance improvement plan starts Monday', 'I will personally sound the horn of Gondor') concern fictional entities with no sincere real-world claim and were not logged.

Re-run of an ADHD explainer written around 2023 ('For me, in 2023, the above still holds'). Mostly present-state clinical claims and normative advice; four items logged, two of them borderline (a content promise and a present-state Talkspace remark).

Short news reaction to the FTC report on PBM generic markups. One hedged conditional about the incoming administration yanking the PBM safe harbor; one indirect statement about PBM executives' comfort.

Interview excerpt about parenting and screens with Carlene MacMillan and the twins for the Parent Tech Action Coalition. No forward-looking claims by the author about the world; Carlene's 'He will use it less' is hers and about the family.

Essay on academic fraud incentives (Ariely, Gino, Wakefield, Elsevier). Gino's book blurb ('the future belongs to the rebel') is quoted mockingly and not logged. Wishes about media coverage of replicators are not logged.
Clozapine history and advocacy. The calls are normative ('we should move to clozapine next', 'Clinicians should reduce the delay') with no predictive reading; quoted trial results are past analysis.
Poem published on the day of the TikTok shutdown (2025-01-19). One hedged call that Trump may resurrect TikTok; one self-referential line about the poem's commercial prospects.

Same-day follow-up after TikTok came back. Calls about Trump's coming action and its legal basis, a trivial 'videos celebrating' call, a judgment about how the episode will be remembered, and one joke about the author's own videos (sincere false).

statements.quote: But that’s for another substack post…
statements.context: In an aside ('My Opinion: Abolish imprisonment...') inside the ADHD explainer, the author promises a future newsletter post on prison abolition. Content promise about The Frontier Psychiatrists.
statements.note: Trivial content promise; about the author's own newsletter (CONTROL candidate). The article is a re-run, so the promise may date from the original 2023 version.

statements.quote: This therapy is not widely available, many therapists are not trained on it and I am highly skeptical any of those therapists are who you will match with on Talkspace.
statements.context: On organizational skills training (OST), the one psychotherapy the author says is effective for ADHD executive dysfunction. He doubts that Talkspace users will be matched with OST-trained therapists.
statements.note: Borderline: reads as a present-state claim about Talkspace's therapist pool despite the future tense 'will match'. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: The next generation of treatments are exciting. They promise better efficacy and a lower side effect profile.
statements.context: 'My Opinion' block right after the author lists promising novel ADHD treatments under research: transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), the recently FDA-approved Monarch eTNS device, and LSD derivatives in clinical trials with Mind Medicine as sponsor. He expects these next-generation treatments to deliver better efficacy and fewer side effects.
statements.note: Compound claim (efficacy and side-effect profile). Author discloses in footnote 9 that he is a MindMed shareholder. Re-run article originally written around 2023.

statements.quote: For me, in 2023, the above still holds. We need more evidence and novel treatments, and as you can see above, they're coming
statements.context: After quoting a 2013 review on alpha agonists (clonidine, guanfacine) that ends 'a long-acting form of clonidine ... is in the process of being developed for use in ADHD', the author endorses it and says novel ADHD treatments and more evidence are coming.
statements.note: Endorsed restatement of the 2013 review's development claim plus the author's own general expectation. Written in 2023 and re-published 2025-01-15.

statements.quote: someone might decide to yank the safe harbor that makes this otherwise completely illegal activity completely legal, and then just let the chips fall they may
statements.context: Reacting to the FTC report that CVS Caremark, Express Scripts and Optum Rx marked up specialty generics by $7.3 billion (2017-2022). Setup: 'If I was in an incoming administration, that had already demonstrated some hostility towards Pharmacy Benefit Managers, and I was trying to slash expenses?' The author speculates the administration might remove the PBM rebate safe harbor.
statements.note: Hedged conditional; the author immediately adds 'I don't know. It's not up to me.' The safe harbor refers to the anti-kickback safe harbor for PBM rebates.

statements.quote: But if I had been that chief executive officer of a PBM subsidiary of a major payer who has been accused of lying to Congress , I might be a little less comfortable today than I was the prior day.
statements.context: Closing thought after the FTC report: the author implies that PBM executives (one accused of lying to Congress) now face greater political and legal risk.
statements.note: Indirect: phrased as present discomfort ('today'), the implied call is rising trouble for PBM executives. Borderline forward-looking.

statements.quote: my article is still working its way into the journal
statements.context: The author mentions he had to issue a correction this past year about retracted MDMA papers and that his correction article is still in the publication pipeline; he expects it to appear.
statements.note: Trivial; about the author's own academic publication (journal unnamed).

statements.quote: Although it will be hard for Andrew Wakefield to get another academic gig
statements.context: Discussing Andrew Wakefield's retracted 1998 Lancet MMR-autism paper; the author expects Wakefield will find it hard to get another academic position.
statements.note: First clause of a compound sentence; the second clause is logged separately.

statements.quote: most academic fraud will never be discovered—the most likely outcome for fraudsters is a long and successful career
statements.context: Essay on incentives for academic fraud (Ariely, Gino, Wakefield, paid authorship, Elsevier margins). The author predicts most fraud stays undetected and fraudsters typically enjoy long, successful careers.
statements.note: Compound general claim about academic fraud detection and fraudsters' careers; not about a specific named event.

statements.quote: And he might even be responsible for her eventual death
statements.context: On Andrew Wakefield's relationship with Elle Macpherson, who was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2018 while with Wakefield, 'a strong advocate of this ideology'. The author speculates that Wakefield's anti-mainstream-medicine influence could contribute to Macpherson's eventual death.
statements.note: Speculative and hedged; concerns a public figure's health outcome. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: It’s possible TikTok will be Jesus-like, resurrected, if not by God, then by The D*nald.
statements.context: Opening of a poem written 'in memory of TikTok' on 2025-01-19, the day the app went dark under the US divest-or-ban law. The author says Donald Trump ('The D*nald') may bring TikTok back.
statements.note: Satirical religious framing but a sincere hedged expectation. Followed by the question 'Will a new religion spring forth?', which is not logged.

statements.quote: A commercial hit, It will not be.
statements.context: The author says his TikTok eulogy poem will not be a commercial hit, contrasting poetry with money-making video content; he then plugs his poetry books.
statements.note: Self-deprecating call about the author's own work (newsletter; CONTROL candidate).

statements.quote: He's gonna do something, that's gonna have some dubious legal basis, but who cares.
statements.context: Same-day follow-up after Trump's 'early morning Sunday magic' brought TikTok back online. 'He' is Donald Trump; the author expects Trump to take an action on TikTok that rests on a dubious legal basis.
statements.note: Compound: Trump will act, and the action's legal basis will be dubious. Post date 2025-01-19, the day before the inauguration.

statements.context: After TikTok's return the author predicts users will post videos celebrating it.

statements.quote: Honestly, this may go down in the annals of the most pointless lawmaking, and law undoing, that I can possibly imagine.
statements.context: On the TikTok ban saga: Congress passed the law, the Supreme Court upheld it, and the president then unilaterally dismissed its impact. The author expects the episode to be remembered as among the most pointless lawmaking and law-undoing.
statements.note: Soft call about future historical judgment rather than a checkable event. Borderline.

statements.quote: I need to go make some videos about UnitedHealth Group that will be a Hit in the Philippines.
statements.context: Closing joke: the author says he will make TikTok videos about UnitedHealth Group that will be a hit in the Philippines.
statements.note: Joke about the author's own content; does not read as a real expectation. Logged with sincere false for recall.
